chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Mis'mam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I gave a man dirhams to perform Hajj on my behalf, and some remained from them, and he did not return them to me. He said: 'They are for him, perhaps he constrained himself regarding the travel expenses due to his need for the expenses.'

key_terms.يَحُجُّ بِهَا عَنِّي: performs Hajj on my behalf (proxy pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the leftover money from a proxy Hajj if the agent keeps it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the disposition of surplus funds in a proxy Hajj, ruling that the agent retains the excess as compensation for any additional personal expenses (*nafakah*) incurred during the journey. This reflects the Shia juristic principle that unless specified otherwise, the agent is entitled to keep the remainder to offset the financial burden of performing the ritual on behalf of the principal, emphasizing fairness in agency contracts (*wakalah*).
